title: Chart.js Small Examples
description: Use these small Chart.js examples with the tools described in each lesson. Read the expected result before you try a change.

examples.title: Create a bar chart
examples.description: A bar chart compares amounts between categories.
examples.output: Two bars compare 3 books on Monday with 5 on Tuesday.

examples.title: Name a dataset
examples.description: A dataset label explains what a set of values measures.
examples.output: The legend names the values Plants watered.

examples.title: Use a line for ordered change
examples.description: A line chart can show how a value changes across an ordered sequence, such as days.
examples.output: Straight line segments connect the reading minutes in day order.

examples.title: Show parts of one total
examples.description: A doughnut chart shows shares of a total.
examples.output: Stories make half of the total of ten books.

examples.title: Plot pairs with a scatter chart
examples.description: A scatter chart places each item using an x value and a y value.
examples.output: Three points show page counts against reading minutes.

examples.title: Choose an honest baseline
examples.description: A bar's length should make comparisons clear.
examples.output: The chart shows that 20 plants is only a little more than 18.

examples.title: Compare two datasets
examples.description: Two datasets can share the same categories.
examples.output: Each day has two bars so the book types can be compared.

examples.title: Update data without making a new chart
examples.description: A chart instance can receive changed data.

examples.title: Fit a sized container
examples.description: A responsive chart uses its parent container to decide its display size.
examples.output: The chart can resize with its dedicated holder while keeping the configured height.

examples.title: Turn off unnecessary animation
examples.description: Chart animation can be disabled when it is not useful.
examples.output: The chart draws directly without an animated transition.

examples.title: Provide text outside the canvas
examples.description: Canvas drawings do not contain normal readable HTML rows.
examples.output: The chart has an accessible name and a visible text summary of the exact values.

examples.title: Destroy an unused chart
examples.description: A chart can keep event listeners and drawing resources.
examples.output: Calling removeChart cleans up the instance and its container.
